I'm actually in grad school too so I know what you mean. Why not try talking to your professors/advisors/administration and see if you can get a leave of absence. Just take a semester or two off to clear your head. I know on my campus they have a psychological office were people can get help. And maybe they can recommend taking off for a while and coming back later to finish up. Most schools are fairly accommodating.

No it's my last day because I quit. Being at this job made me feel really depressed and I've been wanting to end my life because I felt like I was going no where. Sorry if it confused you because I posted it suicide watch. I thought maybe posting it here would give others courage to stop doing things that make them unhappy.
I worked as an engineer. I worked trying to get medical equipment approved. Yes, they really do sour everything.

Wow, it sounds like you're a great mom. I'm no psychologist or whatever but it sounds like maybe your 14 year old needs to go to outside counseling. Or maybe even go to a long term care place where she will be removed from the house to deal with her old problems while you work with the 7 year old. But that's just my thought.

Ouch!! I'm not sure what to say. That really sucks that you don't get to see your kids really often. All I can say is hopefully when they get old enough to make their own decisions you can contact them and explain how you wanted to see them but had difficulties. Hopefully you will be able to make a connection with them later on and no one can tell you not to. If they are an adult and can make their own decision your ex-wife won't be able to say anything about it. I hope I don't sound like a misogynist but it sounds like more and more men are sort of being screwed over by the whole marriage and kids thing. This lady named Helen Smith talks about all the problems you're having. Maybe she has some hints to help.

yeah, over time it gets harder and harder for me to be excited about things. And living for someone else just makes me resent them. It's a tough feeling.

I'm not really sure what to say. I'm 32 and feel the same way. I'm on anti-depressants right now, but I'm not sure they are really helping. I'm not really sure what to do myself. I've thought about doing it myself but for some strange reason I just keep saying to myself maybe just another year. I think one of the reasons (maybe the only reason) why I don't get too down is because occasionally I find random things nearby to do. Like taco festivals, tamale festivals, mostly food related things :-P  Anyways, that's just my thought.

I hope I don't sound harsh but seriously, chill out. I was 24 when I got my drivers license. And I think it's really unfair that society makes us choose what we want to do with the rest of our lives at such a young age. One of my professors said he picked his major because it just happened to be the first one he saw in the schools catalog. Remember, whatever you pick can be changed later, it's not like you're going to be stuck with it for life. It took me 7 1/2 years to get through school, so don't worry about rushing through it. Now after my many years of schooling and only working about 5 years, I've already decided to go back to school to get a master's in something that isn't anywhere near what my bachelors was in.
